hypothesis: Sixteen chains improve mean returned-board accuracy by at least 0.1 percentage point over four chains at a fixed maximum envelope of 16777216 chain moves per puzzle.
primary_statistic: Paired returned-board accuracy difference c16 minus c4, averaged over six search seeds and 10000 shared puzzles at the final maximum chain-move envelope.
decision: Supported if paired two-sided 95% lower endpoint is at least +0.1 pp and zero wrong stops; falsified if upper endpoint is below +0.1 pp or a wrong stop occurs; otherwise inconclusive.
validation: Eight native general, captured general and captured sparse parity checks per job with its assigned chain count. Recompute integer fields and energies at all checkpoints and audit saved boards independently.
limits: Equal maximum chain-move envelope is not equal actual work: early stopping, compaction and check granularity differ; record wall time descriptively.
Annealing period is fixed at 524288 moves per chain; cycle counts differ as part of the resource allocation intervention.
Follow-up slice was unused in the preceding research experiments but belongs to the corpus used by the original reproduction.
Six search seeds, one fixed count graph, no independent training replication.
The 1-chain arm and earlier envelope checkpoints are descriptive; only the final 16-versus-4 comparison is primary.
Random streams are not trajectory-matched across chain counts; comparisons pair common input identities and seed labels.
budget_unit: All checkpoints and endpoints specify maximum chains times moves per chain, not moves per chain.
